_comment: Translator context for en.json / en.manual.json keys: key -> one sentence saying which surface the string appears on and which sense of the English is meant. A SIDECAR, never inline. VS Code's translation key is `message + "/" + comment`, so adding or editing an inline comment there orphans every existing translation of that string; a separate file makes a description free to write and improve at any time. GNOME/KDE reach the same conclusion from the freeze side: "addition of a comment aimed for translators" is exempt from a string freeze, but "adding a context marker (msgctxt) is also subject to the freeze as it renders the affected string 'fuzzy'". Add an entry whenever a key's English is shorter than its meaning - an abbreviation, a bare unit, a key cap, or a word that is both a noun and a verb. Do NOT add one for a sentence fragment (`of`, `at`, `by`, `via`): a fragment needs deleting in Phase 3, and describing it only legitimises it. Coverage of the opaque class is ratcheted by contextSidecar.test.ts.

entries.app.cpu: Abbreviation for "CPU" in the dashboard header's resource strip, followed by a percentage. Width-constrained: keep it as short as the target language allows.
entries.app.dsk: Abbreviation for "disk" in the dashboard header's resource strip, followed by a percentage. Width-constrained: keep it as short as the target language allows.
entries.app.mem: Abbreviation for "memory" (RAM) in the dashboard header's resource strip, followed by a percentage. Width-constrained: keep it as short as the target language allows.
entries.app.v: The "v" that prefixes a version number, rendered immediately before the digits with no space (`v1.2.3`). Most languages leave this untranslated.
entries.apps.autoImprovement.findingDetail.red: The gate stage named "RED": the reproducing test FAILS on unmodified code, which is what proves the defect is real. A protocol token the app also prints in logs and commit notes, so keep the Latin form; it is not the colour.
entries.apps.autoResearch.researchLabPage.30s: A preset duration of 30 seconds. The number is data; only the unit letter is translatable, and most locales keep `s`.
entries.apps.autoResearch.researchLabPage.60s: A preset duration of 60 seconds. The number is data; only the unit letter is translatable, and most locales keep `s`.
entries.apps.autoResearch.researchLabPage.add: Verb on the button that adds the typed sub-question to the research list beside it. If the target language needs an object, name the sub-question. Distinct from the "Add" on the Code Review Sage page, which adds a review pattern.
entries.apps.autoResearch.researchLabPage.min: The unit "min" = minutes, rendered after a number. An abbreviation, not the word "minimum".
entries.apps.codeReviewSage.components.addReposM: Button on the add-repositories dialog. A VERB: adds the typed repository to the app's pinned set. Not the noun 'an add'.
entries.apps.codeReviewSage.components.bandChips: Filter chip above the report's findings list. Means 'no band filter — show every severity', not 'all' as a quantity.
Version chip in the app rail's identity row, e.g. "v2.0". `{{version}}` is the number — keep the prefix short, and drop it entirely if your locale does not prefix version numbers.
entries.apps.codeReviewSage.components.prPickLis: Badge on a pull request in the picker, marking one that appeared since the last review of this repository. An ADJECTIVE describing the pull request.
entries.apps.codeReviewSage.components.reviewCha: Speaker label above the reader's own question in the Code Review Sage chat transcript, paired with "Reviewer" for the agent's replies; the second-person pronoun addressing the current user, not the possessive "your".
entries.apps.crewCompanion.breathe.end: Label on the button that stops the breathing exercise before it finishes, inside the exercise overlay. An imperative verb ("stop this now"), not the noun "the end" — several languages use different words for the two.
entries.apps.crewCompanion.header.desktop_tip: Hint under the Crew Companion page subtitle when the desktop overlay is running. Tells the user they can click the sprite to open its panel and right-click to change its avatar. It must NOT tell them to quit from that menu: turning the companion off is now a button on this page.
entries.apps.crewCompanion.menu.quit: Label shared by the pet's right-click menu item and the Turn off button on the Crew Companion dashboard page. Both POST the app-disable endpoint. An imperative verb ("stop it now"), not the adjective "disabled".
entries.apps.crewCompanion.offline.couldnt_turn_: Failure notice after the Crew Companion page's Turn off button cannot reach POST /api/apps/crew-companion/disable. {{error}} is the server's reason. Same shape as couldnt_open.
entries.apps.crewCompanion.reminders.add_button: Button that saves the reminder typed in the box beside it. The verb "add", not the arithmetic sense.
entries.apps.crewCompanion.settings.custom_place: Placeholder in a small number field for a custom break interval. Short for "minutes" (the unit), not "minimum".
entries.apps.crewCompanion.time.now: Relative time label on a reminder that is due at this moment, shown where others read "20 min from now".
entries.apps.crewCompanion.view.everyMinShort: Placeholder inside the small number field for a CUSTOM break interval, in the companion panel's break-rhythm row beside the 30/45/60/90 preset buttons. Short for "minutes" (the unit), not "minimum". The field is only as wide as two or three digits, so keep it to the shortest form the target language has.
entries.apps.designCritique.askLayer.ask: Verb on the submit button of the "ask about this" popover in Design Critique: send the typed question about the highlighted finding. Not the noun ("an ask").
entries.apps.designCritique.composer.unrecognise: Design Critique composer, said back to the user about what they just pasted: the input is not a Figma link, a code repository, an absolute local path or a serving URL. Describes the pasted reference, not the critique or the user, so an adjective agreeing with a masculine or feminine noun should agree with the local word for the pasted link or path.
entries.apps.designCritique.composer.critique_th: Label of the button that starts a critique on the Design Critique composer, shown once two or more screenshots are staged. The count is how many are staged, and the critique covers the order they are in as well as each screen.
Label of the button that starts a critique on the Design Critique composer, shown when exactly one screenshot is staged.
entries.apps.designCritique.designCritiquePage.s: Last-resort error text used only when the thrown exception carries no message of its own. It is rendered alone on the composer's error line, so it has to read as a complete notice even though the English is lower-case.
Client-side timeout during the discovery pass that finds screens behind a Figma link, a repository or a running URL, before any reviewing starts. The pass keeps going server-side.

Client-side timeout notice for the critique the user is watching: the run was not cancelled and continues on the server, so this must not be phrased as a failure. The shorter of two sibling timeout notices — this one drops the promise about resuming.

The same timeout situation as the sibling key ending in `_come`, reached from the background poll rather than the foreground run, which is why this variant also tells the user that coming back later resumes it.
entries.apps.designCritique.designCritiquePage.t: Fallback error for a failed review run with no message of its own. "Critique" is this app's noun for one review of one design, and is used as a countable noun throughout.
Rejection when more than twenty screenshots are sent in one go. "Screens" here means app screens or screenshots, never physical displays or monitors.
Fallback error for a failed discovery pass with no message of its own. "Scan" is that pass over a link, repo or URL looking for screens — nothing to do with security scanning.
Rejection shown when every file the user dropped or picked was filtered out for not having an image MIME type, so nothing was staged at all.
entries.apps.designCritique.designCritiquePage.n: Verb-like button in the Design Critique rail header: start a new critique. The create sense, not a "recently added" badge.
entries.apps.designTweak.devServer.use: Verb on the button that accepts the dev-server URL typed (or detected) beside it, so Design Tweak frames the preview from that server. Not the noun "use" and not "usage".
entries.apps.designTweak.projects.add: Verb on the button that registers the folder path typed beside it as a web app Design Tweak can preview. If the target language needs an object, name the app or folder.
entries.apps.designTweak.projects.dev_badge: Badge on a project row in Design Tweak's app dropdown, marking an app that is previewed from its running dev server. Short for "development server" and rendered lowercase; most locales keep the English `dev`, which is what the surrounding UI calls it.
entries.apps.issueRadar.components.labelPicker.a: Verb on a button: add an entry to the list beside it. If the target language needs an object, name the thing being added.
entries.apps.issueRadar.components.leftRail.v: The "v" that prefixes a version number, rendered immediately before the digits with no space (`v1.2.3`). Most languages leave this untranslated.
entries.apps.issueRadar.components.prBulkBar.mer: Confirmation line before an irreversible bulk merge, naming the exact pull requests and the merge strategy. `numbers` is a pre-formatted list of provider references (`#7, #8 and #9` on GitHub, `!7, !8 and !9` on GitLab) - do not translate or re-punctuate it. `method` is a Git merge STRATEGY name (`squash`) - keep it verbatim.
entries.apps.issueRadar.connectPanel.cli: "CLI" = command-line interface, naming a connection method the user picks. Keep the acronym practitioners in the target language use.
entries.apps.issueRadar.views.crews.editor.label: Chip at the end of the owned-labels row in the crew editor, which opens the label picker. A VERB in the sense of "attach another label to this crew's scope" — not the noun, and not arithmetic. It sits beside real label names, so it must read as an action rather than as one more label.
entries.apps.issueRadar.views.crews.filter_all: First chip in the crew list's filter row, beside Working / Needs you / Paused. Means "no state filter — show every crew, including paused and retired ones", not "all" as a quantity or "whole".
entries.apps.issueRadar.views.crews.page.kind_ci: Badge on a line of a crew's work log, naming what that entry recorded: a continuous-integration run on the crew's pull request. "CI" = continuous integration — keep the acronym practitioners in the target language use, and keep it short: the badge sits in a fixed-width column beside longer labels like "Merged" and "Handed back".
entries.apps.issueRadar.views.settings.generalSe: Section HEADING (a noun: 'the refresh settings'), not the verb. The nearby repoSettings.refresh IS the verb on a button — five languages already translate the two differently, so do not reuse one word for both.
entries.apps.issueRadar.views.tagging.untaggedIs: Verb on a button: add an entry to the list beside it. If the target language needs an object, name the thing being added.
entries.apps.meetings.priority.low: Priority level of a meeting action item, the lowest of high/medium/low. An adjective describing importance, not volume or position.
entries.apps.meetings.settings.addTerm: Verb on a button: add a term to the meeting dictionary (the vocabulary list that improves transcription accuracy). If the target language needs an object, "add a term" is the sense.
entries.apps.meetings.taskSidebar.add: Verb on a button: add an entry to the list beside it. If the target language needs an object, name the thing being added.
entries.apps.mochi.approval.bubble_needs_approva: Speech bubble floating over the desktop pet when a tool is waiting on the user. {{pet}} is the pet's name, which the user can change in Settings, so it must stay a placeholder and must not be translated. {{purpose}} is a free-text sentence the AI agent wrote about what it is trying to do; it can be long, so keep the surrounding words short. The bubble is narrow.

Same desktop speech bubble as apps.mochi.approval.bubble_needs_approval, used when the agent stated no purpose. {{pet}} is the user-chosen pet name (do not translate). Keep it short: the bubble is narrow.
entries.apps.mochi.approval.risk_low: The LOW end of the risk scale (low / medium / high) on the pet's tool-approval dialog, rendered immediately before the word "risk". An adjective describing how dangerous the pending action is, not height or volume.
entries.apps.mochi.approval.trust_all_base: Button granting standing permission for a whole command family, e.g. every 'npm' command. {{base}} is one or more command names joined by ', ' (a piped command yields several). Middle of three trust options: wider than trust_this_command, narrower than trust_all_tools.
entries.apps.mochi.approval.trust_all_tools: Button granting standing permission for EVERY tool in this chat, not just the one being asked about. Widest of the three trust options — the wording should feel broader than trust_this_command and trust_all_base.
entries.apps.mochi.approval.trust_this_command: Button granting standing permission for ONE exact command. {{cmd}} is that command, shown verbatim in a monospace-ish label and already shortened with an ellipsis if long. Narrowest of three trust options; must read as narrower than apps.mochi.approval.trust_all_base and trust_all_tools.
entries.apps.mochi.settingsPanel.mcp_add: Button that adds a new MCP server row in the desktop pet's Settings window. The VERB "add", not the noun.
entries.apps.mochi.sprite.fps: Abbreviation for "frames per second", labelling a number input in the pet's spritesheet importer. Keep the conventional abbreviation for the target language rather than expanding it; the field is width-constrained.
entries.apps.mochi.watchPanel.priority.low: The LOW end of a watch item's priority scale (high / normal / low) in the pet's watch list. An adjective describing importance, not height or volume.
entries.apps.opsMissionControl.opsMissionControl: Autonomy-mode badge for the highest level, where the agent executes actions its rules grant. The imperative verb "act", one of three modes with "observe" and "propose"; not the noun ("an act").
entries.apps.opsMissionControl.settingsPanel.gh: The literal name of the GitHub CLI executable, `gh`, shown in monospace. Do not translate: the user types it.
entries.apps.opsMissionControl.settingsPanel.min: The unit "min" = minutes, rendered after a number in a staleness-timeout field. An abbreviation, not the word "minimum".
entries.apps.opsMissionControl.settingsPanel.mod: Label on the third segment of the autonomy-mode control in Ops Mission Control Settings, where the agent executes actions its rules grant. The imperative verb "act", alongside "Observe" and "Propose"; not the noun ("an act").
entries.apps.opsMissionControl.settingsPanel.off: State value meaning disabled, on a notification-channel or sync badge. Not the preposition or the adverb.
entries.apps.opsMissionControl.settingsPanel.who: The literal `who:` key of an on-call shift entry in the committed rotation.yaml file, shown in monospace. Do not translate: it names a YAML field the user edits.
entries.apps.papyrus.page.pdf: The file format "PDF", labelling the compiled output of a LaTeX paper. An acronym practitioners keep untranslated in nearly every locale.
entries.apps.papyrus.workspace.log: Noun: the LaTeX compiler's output log, naming a tab beside the PDF preview. A record of what the compiler printed — NOT the verb "to log" and not a logarithm.
entries.apps.personalShopper.preferencesTab.add: Submit button on the inline 'add a preference' form in the Personal Shopper Preferences tab. The VERB (commit this new preference), not the noun 'an addition'. The sibling add_group is the same verb applied to a group, so a language that inflects by object may need a different form.
entries.apps.pptxMaker.libraryPanel.font_specime: Type specimen shown large in the template preview, filled with that template's own theme font and text colour. Not a label: the two characters exist so the user can judge the TYPEFACE's letterforms at a glance, the role an "Aa" ramp plays in a font picker. Keep the Latin pair unless your readers would judge a typeface better from one upper- and one lower-case glyph of their own script; never render it as a word.
entries.apps.specBuilder.components.projectPicke: Spec Builder's project-folder picker: the button that navigates one directory level up. 'Up' means the parent folder, not upward motion or an increase.
entries.apps.specBuilder.components.specRail.v: Spec Builder's sidebar footer: the single-letter prefix before the app version number, as in v1.2.3. Short for version, not the letter itself.
entries.apps.workflows.workflowsPage.run: Verb on a button: execute this job/workflow now. NOT the noun ("a run"), which several locales translate differently.
entries.autoImprovement.prTitlePrefix: "PR" = pull request, prefixing a generated pull-request title. Keep the abbreviation the target language's developers actually use; do not expand it if that would break the layout.
entries.components.appstore.featureCard.get: Verb on an App Store button: install this app. Not the sense of obtain or receive.
entries.components.appstore.featuredSpotlight.ge: Verb on an App Store button: install this app. Not the sense of obtain or receive.
entries.components.appstore.featuredSpotlight.v: The "v" that prefixes a version number, rendered immediately before the digits with no space (`v1.2.3`). Most languages leave this untranslated.
entries.components.appstore.installedAppCard.v: The "v" that prefixes a version number, rendered immediately before the digits with no space (`v1.2.3`). Most languages leave this untranslated.
entries.components.chatInput.queue_run_after_the: Description under the Queue option in the busy composer's send menu. 'Current work' can be either a live response or background sub-agents, so do not narrow it to the current turn.
Tooltip for the busy composer's Queue action. It waits until all current work is finished; `Enter` names the keyboard key and must stay verbatim.
entries.components.chatInput.steer_act_on_this_a: Tooltip for the busy composer's Steer action. It injects into a live response, or starts a new response when only background sub-agents are running; translate the broader promise to act as soon as possible. `Enter` names the keyboard key and must stay verbatim.
entries.components.chatInput.steer_act_on_this_r: Description under the Steer option in the busy composer's send menu. It means act on the message now, whether that injects into a live response or starts a new response while background sub-agents continue.
entries.components.commandPalette.providers.allA: Section heading in Search Everywhere for the aggregated result list that mixes every provider (pages, sessions, skills, prompts…). Means "all categories", not "everything selected".
entries.components.commandPalette.tab: The literal Tab key cap, shown inside a key badge. Do not translate or transliterate: it names a physical key the user presses.
entries.components.crewWakeSection.active: Status word on a schedule row in the crew editor: the job is enabled and will fire. An adjective describing the schedule, not a verb and not "activate". Width-constrained: keep it short.
entries.components.crewWakeSection.paused: Status word on a schedule row in the crew editor: the job exists but is suspended and will not fire until resumed. An adjective, not the verb "pause". Width-constrained: keep it short.
entries.components.crewWakeSection.running: Status word on a schedule row in the crew editor: a run of this job is in flight right now. An adjective describing the schedule's current state, not a command. Width-constrained: keep it short.
entries.components.discoverySearchBar.no: Answer/state value meaning negative. Not the beginning of a phrase such as "No results".
entries.components.executionsView.ok: Status value in a table or log line, meaning the operation succeeded. A state, not the confirmation button.
entries.components.filePickerMenu.folder: aria-label on the folder ICON in the @-mention picker row and on the staged-folder chip in the composer. A directory in the file system, not a UI grouping.
entries.components.filePickerMenu.folder_kind: Row metadata in the @-mention picker, rendered as 'folder · 3d ago' where a file row shows '12 KB · 3d ago'. Lowercase noun naming the entry kind (a file-system directory).
entries.components.folderColorNames.red: Display name of the red folder color, interpolated into “Set color to {{name}}” on a swatch in the folder-settings color palette. The color adjective as a noun-like label.
entries.components.jobForm.add: Verb on the submit button of the scheduled-job form: add this job. Shown only when the form is horizontal and owns its own submit control, and it swaps to "Adding…" while the request is in flight. If the target language needs an object, name the job.
entries.components.logEntry.ok: Status value in a table or log line, meaning the operation succeeded. A state, not the confirmation button.
entries.components.mcpBrowserModal.v: The "v" that prefixes a version number, rendered immediately before the digits with no space (`v1.2.3`). Most languages leave this untranslated.
entries.components.mcpCustomServerModal.env: "env" = environment variables, labelling a key/value editor. An abbreviation of a technical term, not the English word "environment" in its ordinary sense.
entries.components.mcpCustomServerModal.url: "URL", labelling an input field. Lowercase because it matches the config key it edits; do not capitalise or translate.
entries.components.notifications.notificationFee: Filter option meaning no filter — show every item. A quantifier over the list beside it, not the adjective "whole".
entries.components.publishHub.kb: The unit "KB" = kilobytes, rendered after a published bundle's size. NOT "knowledge base", which is a separate feature in this product that shares the abbreviation in English.
entries.components.readingWidthToggle.label_full: One-letter button cap for the FULL reading width (chat spans the whole pane). Sits beside the M cap. Use the initial of the target language's word for "full/wide"; keep it to one character so the two caps stay the same size.
entries.components.readingWidthToggle.label_md: One-letter button cap for the MEDIUM reading width (chat is column-constrained for readability). Sits beside the F cap. Use the initial of the target language's word for "medium"; keep it to one character.
entries.components.remoteArtifactCard.v: The "v" that prefixes a version number, rendered immediately before the digits with no space (`v1.2.3`). Most languages leave this untranslated.
entries.components.runInTerminalConfirm.run: Verb on a button: execute this job/workflow now. NOT the noun ("a run"), which several locales translate differently.
entries.components.searchResultsList.you: Speaker label on a search result whose message came from the user rather than the agent — the second-person pronoun as a NAME for the author, the way a chat transcript labels a turn. Not the object "you" in a sentence.
entries.components.sessionActionsMenu.pin: Verb on a menu item that pins the session to the top of the sidebar. Paired with "Unpin" on the same item, which is why it is a bare verb rather than "Pin session".
entries.components.shortcutsModal.global_hotkey_: Help text under the desktop app's system-wide summon shortcut. `globalHotkey` is a literal JSON config key and `Connection > Open Config File` is a literal (untranslated) menu path in the desktop app — leave both exactly as written.
entries.components.shortcutsModal.k: The literal letter on the keyboard's K key, shown inside a key cap next to a modifier (`Cmd + K`). Do not translate or transliterate: it names a physical key.
entries.components.shortcutsModal.show_or_focus_: Label for the OS-level shortcut that brings the Kiro Crew desktop window to the front from any application. 'Kiro Crew' is the product name — do not translate.
entries.components.themeEditor.var_aim: Row label in the theme editor for the `--aim` colour token. AIM is this project's name for the agent-activity accent — an opaque token name, not the English word "aim". Keep it verbatim in every language.
entries.components.themeEditor.var_ok: Row label in the theme editor for the `--ok` colour token: the success/healthy colour, shown beside Warning, Danger and Info. Names the colour role, not an acknowledgement — many languages keep "OK".
entries.components.trustDropdown.trust_all_base: Menu item granting standing permission for a whole command family. {{base}} is one or more command names joined by ', ' and must stay inside the <mono> tag. Middle of three trust options: wider than trust_this_command, narrower than trust_all_tools.
entries.components.trustDropdown.trust_this_comm: Menu item granting standing permission for ONE exact command. {{cmd}} is shown verbatim, already shortened when long, and must stay inside the <mono> tag. Narrowest of the three trust options.
entries.components.voiceDictationPanel.esc_to_ca: Keyboard hint in the corner of the voice dictation panel for BATCH speech-to-text: the user must click the mic to stop and transcribe. 'Esc' is a physical key name. Width-constrained: keep it short.

Keyboard hint in the corner of the voice dictation panel. 'Esc' and 'Enter' are physical key names -- use the conventional key names printed on keyboards for this locale. Width-constrained: keep it short.
entries.components.voiceDictationPanel.listening: Status label on the voice dictation panel while the microphone is capturing. Present participle describing the app's current state, not a command to the user.
entries.lib.effort.low: Reasoning-effort level in the chat model picker: the least thinking time, fastest answers. An adjective naming an amount of effort, not a volume or a priority.
entries.lib.effort.max: Reasoning-effort level in the chat model picker: the highest setting the model offers. Short for "maximum" — the top of a scale, not a verb.
entries.pages.agentsPage.id: Column header over the short generated identifier of a spawned subagent run, e.g. "470cf2d9".
entries.pages.agentsPage.status: Column header over a subagent run state: Running, Done or Failed.
entries.pages.agentsPage.task: Column header over the one-line description of what a spawned subagent was asked to do. A noun, not the verb "to task".
entries.pages.appDetailPage.v: The "v" that prefixes a version number, rendered immediately before the digits with no space (`v1.2.3`). Most languages leave this untranslated.
entries.pages.appsPage.v: The "v" that prefixes a version number, rendered immediately before the digits with no space (`v1.2.3`). Most languages leave this untranslated.
entries.pages.artifactDeployPage.aws: The literal name of the AWS CLI executable, `aws`. Do not translate: the user types it.
entries.pages.artifactDetailPage.copy_failed: Brief error status on the artifact content copy button after a clipboard write fails. A past outcome, not a command.
entries.pages.artifactDetailPage.tag_2: Noun: a label attached to an artifact. Not the verb.
entries.pages.artifactDetailPage.v: The "v" that prefixes a version number, rendered immediately before the digits with no space (`v1.2.3`). Most languages leave this untranslated.
entries.pages.artifactsPage.all: Filter option meaning no filter — show every item. A quantifier over the list beside it, not the adjective "whole".
entries.pages.artifactsPage.v: The "v" that prefixes a version number, rendered immediately before the digits with no space (`v1.2.3`). Most languages leave this untranslated.
entries.pages.artifactsPage.ver: Column header abbreviating "version" in the artifacts table. Abbreviated for column width, not for style.
entries.pages.channelPage.add: Verb on a button: add an entry to the list beside it. If the target language needs an object, name the thing being added.
entries.pages.channelPage.listen_all: Badge on a Slack/Discord channel meaning the agent listens to EVERY message in it. Contrasts with the sibling badges 'mention' (only when @-mentioned) and 'silent' (never). Short, sits next to an icon — keep it to one or two words.
entries.pages.channelPage.ok: Status value in a table or log line, meaning the operation succeeded. A state, not the confirmation button.
entries.pages.chat.activityViewer.resource_type_: "PR" = pull request. Keep the abbreviation the target language's developers actually use; do not expand it if that would break the layout.
entries.pages.chat.assistantMessage.raw: Label on the toggle that switches an assistant message from its rendered markdown to the unformatted source text. The adjective "raw" as in raw/unprocessed output, not the verb and not "rare". Paired with the rendered view on the same control, so keep it as short as the target language allows.
entries.pages.chat.pinnedPrompt.jump_to_this_tur: Tooltip on the pinned banner's jump button in the chat transcript. "Turn" means one conversation turn — the pinned opener may be a user prompt, an auto-nudge cycle, or a subagent completion event — not a game move or a waiting-line turn.
entries.pages.chat.pins.you: Attribution label shown below a pinned chat message indicating which user pinned it. "You" means the current user pinned this message themselves.
entries.pages.chat.sessionFlyout.new: Label on the small ACTION BUTTON that starts a new chat session, in the recents flyout that opens on hovering the collapsed session sidebar's toggle. Space is tight (the button sits beside a caption in a ~244px panel), so this is the clipped form of the sibling key `new_chat` ("New chat") - translate it as an imperative button, the sense of 'start a new one', not the adjective 'recently made'. If your language cannot shorten it, reuse the `new_chat` wording; a wrapped button beats a wrong sense.
entries.pages.chat.subagentProgressBar.s: The unit "s" = seconds, rendered directly after a number (`30s`). Not a plural marker.
entries.pages.chat.toolDetails.raw: Segment label on the tool-call details panel, paired with "Formatted". Selects the unprocessed payload -- the exact bytes the agent sent or received, with escape sequences left as written -- rather than the prettified table view. "Raw" as in unprocessed data, not uncooked food. Keep it to one short word if the language allows; it sits in a two-segment toggle.
entries.pages.chatPage.open_folder: aria-label and tooltip on the folder chip inside a SENT chat message. Clicking opens that directory in the side panel's file tree; {{path}} is the absolute directory path. Mirror the phrasing of pages.chatPage.open_file.
entries.pages.chatSidebar.min: The unit "min" = minutes, rendered after a number. An abbreviation, not the word "minimum".
entries.pages.chatSidebar.new: Label on the "+" button in the chat sidebar header that starts a new chat. entries.pages.devFleetPage.mb: The unit "MB" = megabytes, rendered after a numeric size.
entries.pages.devFleetPage.pod: A Kiro Crew dev "pod" — an isolated development environment. Product terminology; see the do-not-translate glossary before translating.
entries.pages.devFleetPage.pod_2: A Kiro Crew dev "pod" — an isolated development environment. Product terminology; see the do-not-translate glossary before translating.
entries.pages.devFleetPage.pr: Label introducing a pull-request link. "PR" = pull request; keep the abbreviation the target language's developers use, and keep the colon.
entries.pages.devFleetPage.pr_2: "PR" = pull request. Keep the abbreviation the target language's developers actually use; do not expand it if that would break the layout.
entries.pages.hooksPage.ms: The unit "ms" = milliseconds, rendered after a duration. Use the abbreviation your locale's technical writing uses.
entries.pages.hooksPage.ok: Status value in a table or log line, meaning the operation succeeded. A state, not the confirmation button.
entries.pages.hooksPage.s: The unit "s" = seconds, rendered directly after a number (`30s`). Not a plural marker.
entries.pages.knowledge.index.esc: The literal Esc key cap. Do not translate unless the target locale's keyboards are genuinely labelled differently: it names a physical key.
entries.pages.mcpGatewayCard.pid: "PID" = operating-system process id, labelling a number. A term of art; keep the acronym practitioners in the target language use.
entries.pages.mcpGatewayCard.rss: "RSS" = resident set size, the process's physical memory use, labelling a byte count. NOT the web feed format.
entries.pages.mcpGatewayCard.s: The unit "s" = seconds, rendered directly after a number (`30s`). Not a plural marker.
entries.pages.overview.memoryTab.add: Verb on a button: add an entry to the list beside it. If the target language needs an object, name the thing being added.
entries.pages.overview.portabilityTab.kb: The unit "KB" = kilobytes, rendered after a numeric size. NOT "knowledge base", which is a separate feature in this product that shares the abbreviation in English.
entries.pages.overview.tokenDailyChart.all: Filter option meaning no filter — show every item. A quantifier over the list beside it, not the adjective "whole".
entries.pages.overview.tokenDailyChart.in: Label for the number of input tokens in a chart tooltip, paired with the sibling "Out:". "In" is short for input, not the preposition.
entries.pages.overview.vectorMemoryCard.all: Filter option meaning no filter — show every item. A quantifier over the list beside it, not the adjective "whole".
entries.pages.overview.vectorMemoryCard.set: Verb on a button: apply this value. NOT the noun ("a set") and not the adjective ("is set").
entries.pages.overviewPage.up: Status value meaning the service is running and reachable. Not the direction.
entries.pages.performanceTab.graph_scale_network: Caption under the network graph. Network is the one self-scaled trace, so the full-scale value must be printed or idle traffic looks identical to a flood. {{max}} is KB/s at full bar height, {{seconds}} the span plotted.
entries.pages.performanceTab.graph_scale_percent: Caption under a CPU/memory/disk graph. Those traces are fixed to a 0-100 scale, so only the time window varies. {{seconds}} is the span currently plotted.
entries.pages.performanceTab.os: Row label on the System page's Performance plane, in the machine-identity strip. Abbreviation of "operating system" - the kernel/distribution string of the host, not a Kiro Crew setting.
entries.pages.performanceTab.resource_cpu: Name of the CPU resource in the Performance plane's left-hand resource picker, and the heading of its graph. Abbreviation of "central processing unit" - the processor as a whole, not one core and not a percentage.
entries.pages.performanceTab.working_directory: Label for the gateway process's current working directory (`cwd`). Deliberately not "checkout": a pip or DMG install has no git worktree, so naming one would be false there.
entries.pages.projectDetailPage.dag: "DAG" = directed acyclic graph, naming the dependency-graph view of a project's tasks. Keep the acronym if that is what practitioners use in the target language.
entries.pages.projectsPage.run: Verb on a button: execute this job/workflow now. NOT the noun ("a run"), which several locales translate differently.
entries.pages.remoteArtifactDetailPage.v: The "v" that prefixes a version number, rendered immediately before the digits with no space (`v1.2.3`). Most languages leave this untranslated.
entries.pages.schedulePage.confirm_delete_job: Label of the row's Delete button in its ARMED state: the first click arms, and this string is what a second click/tap will execute. It must state the destructive action by itself (touch users get no hover tooltip) AND stay very short — the fixed-width actions cell fits roughly the width of the English "Delete?"; a longer value clips the adjacent menu. Phrase as a terse confirmation question using the same verb as the 'delete' key.
entries.pages.schedulePage.cronFolders.job_count: Singular count label in a cron folder header row — means one scheduled cron job, not employment.
Plural count label in a cron folder header row — means multiple scheduled cron jobs, not employment.
entries.pages.schedulePage.id: Column header for a record's identifier in a table. Keep it short; it labels a column of opaque id strings.
entries.pages.schedulePage.new: Verb-like button label: create a new one of these. If the target language needs a noun, name the object being created.
entries.pages.schedulePage.now: Rendered in place of a countdown ("in 5m") when a scheduled job is already due — the time remaining is zero or negative. An adverb of time meaning "at this moment", NOT the "Run now" button on the same page.
entries.pages.schedulePage.ok: Status value in a table or log line, meaning the operation succeeded. A state, not the confirmation button.
entries.pages.schedulePage.run: Verb on a button: execute this job/workflow now. NOT the noun ("a run"), which several locales translate differently.
entries.pages.servicesTab.pid: Row label on the System page's Services plane, for the gateway's operating-system process identifier. Abbreviation of "process ID" - a number the reader copies into `ps` or a task manager, so keep it as the platform abbreviation rather than expanding it.
entries.pages.servicesTab.working_directory: Label for the gateway process's current working directory (`cwd`). Deliberately not "checkout": a pip or DMG install has no git worktree, so naming one would be false there.
entries.pages.sessionsTab.cpu_cores: Sortable column header in the Sessions table, holding a session's processor usage measured in CPU cores (not percent). The parenthetical clarifies the unit.
entries.pages.sessionsTab.cpu_cores_hint: InfoTip that explains the CPU column's unit: cores, not percent. Appears on click of the ? icon beside the header.
entries.pages.sessionsTab.group_app: Option label in the Sessions table's Group-by control, currently greyed out. Short for "application" - a Kiro Crew app (an installed extension such as Dev Fleet or Code Review Sage), NOT a generic program and not a mobile app. It names the attribute the rows would be folded by, so it reads as a noun, not a verb.
entries.pages.sessionsTab.mcp_stubs: Sortable column header in the Sessions table, counting the MCP (Model Context Protocol) stub processes bridging a session to external tool servers. 'MCP' is an abbreviation that should stay abbreviated; 'stubs' are lightweight proxy processes.
entries.pages.sessionsTab.mcp_stubs_hint: InfoTip explaining what an MCP stub process is. Appears on click of the ? icon beside the column header.
entries.pages.sessionsTab.pid: Sortable column header in the Sessions table, holding the operating-system process identifier of the session's agent runtime. Abbreviation of "process ID" - a number the reader copies into `ps` or `kill`, so keep it as the platform abbreviation rather than expanding it.
entries.pages.settings.aboutPanel.v: The "v" that prefixes a version number, rendered immediately before the digits with no space (`v1.2.3`). Most languages leave this untranslated.
entries.pages.settings.instancesPanel.20h: A preset retention/timeout duration of 20 hours. The number is data; only the unit letter is translatable, and most locales keep `h`.
entries.pages.settings.notificationsPanel.app: "app" as a notification-delivery target, meaning the desktop application itself rather than Slack or Discord.
entries.pages.settings.notificationsPanel.test_s: Button in the Sound settings card that plays a sample of the current fallback notification sound at the current volume. "Test" is the VERB (try it out); phrase as an imperative action like the sibling per-category "Test" buttons. It only plays a tone — no notification is created or delivered, which is why the English says "sound".
entries.pages.settings.notificationsPanel.preset: Name of a notification sound preset — a short percussive 'pop'. One of several sound names in a picker; it names the sound, so translate only if the language has a natural onomatopoeia, otherwise keep it.
entries.pages.settings.securityPanel.add: Verb on a button: add an entry to the list beside it. If the target language needs an object, name the thing being added.
entries.pages.settings.securityPanel.off: State value meaning disabled. Not the preposition or the adverb.
entries.pages.settings.securityPanel.tailnet_sta: State badge on the Tailnet origin card meaning the setting is disabled, so no tailnet name is in the dashboard origin allow-list. Sits beside "Active" and "Not resolved" as one of four states. The adjective/state, not the preposition or the adverb.
entries.pages.settings.slackPanel.add: Verb on a button: add an entry to the list beside it. If the target language needs an object, name the thing being added.
entries.pages.settings.sttSettings.dictation_pan: Label for the toggle in Settings > Voice that switches the recording UI between the animated dictation panel and the thin status bar.
entries.pages.settings.sttSettings.show_an_anima: Description under the 'Dictation panel' toggle in Settings > Voice. 'WebGL2' is a technology name and must not be translated. 'reduced motion' refers to the OS accessibility preference.
entries.pages.systemPage.live_system_metrics: Subtitle under the System page title. Deliberately carries no refresh interval: the header is page-level while each plane polls at its own rate (Performance 2s, Sessions 5s), so naming one would be wrong for the others.
entries.pages.telemetryPanel.max_col: Column header on the latency profiles: the single slowest sample recorded. It is the far end of the tail and often orders of magnitude above p90, which is why the axis beside it is logarithmic.
entries.pages.telemetryPanel.min_col: Column header on the latency profiles: the single fastest sample this instrument recorded in the window. It anchors the left end of the log axis, so it is the floor the profile bar is measured from, not a typical value.
entries.pages.telemetryPanel.p50_col: Column header on the latency tables: the median, i.e. half the measured samples finished at or below this duration. "p50" is standard percentile notation and is normally kept verbatim.
entries.pages.telemetryPanel.p90_col: Column header on the latency tables: the slow tail, i.e. nine in ten measured samples finished at or below this duration. This is the figure a reader checks when something feels slow.
entries.pages.telemetryPanel.prior_credits_turns: Sub-line under the 'vs previous period' spend stat: the previous window's totals, e.g. 'credits 500 · turns 50'. 'credits' is the spend unit and 'turns' counts agent turns; both placeholders are pre-formatted numbers. Deliberately label-before-number so the unit words need no plural agreement (the counts can be 1) — keep that order and the middle-dot separator, and use your language's plain label form of each unit.
entries.pages.telemetryPanel.turns_to_compaction: Table cell in the Context tab's 'To 90%' column: the forecast number of agent turns left before the conversation's context reaches 90% and compacts, e.g. '4 turns'. A plural key (the _one form covers the singular): 'turn' is the same unit as the Turns column.
entries.pages.webhooksPage.0_b: Size unit in the Webhooks run detail pane: zero bytes, shown when a run returned no result payload. 'B' abbreviates byte and is not a word.
entries.pages.webhooksPage.run: Noun, not a verb: one recorded execution of an inbound webhook, used as a column heading in the Webhooks run history. Never an instruction to start something.
entries.utils.schedulePresets.category_ops: Category heading in the scheduled-job template gallery. Short for "Operations" -- the group of templates that watch deployments, CI and infrastructure health. A NOUN naming the category, not the verb "to operate". Sits in a row of sibling headings, so keep it about as short as the other category names in your language.
entries.pages.chatSidebar.clear: Label on the destructive button in the chat sidebar's Older Sessions header row. It permanently deletes every closed history session on disk (DELETE /api/sessions), the same removal the per-row "Delete history session" performs, sparing only sessions open in a tab and pinned ones. Translate it with your language's word for permanent deletion, NOT a "clear the list" or "tidy up" verb: the earlier English said "Clear", which read as reversible. Width-constrained: it sits next to a collapse chevron.
entries.pages.chatSidebar.clear_closed_sessions_: Browser confirm() text for the Older Sessions "Delete all" button. Deletion is permanent and irreversible; keep the "cannot be undone" warning explicit rather than leading with what survives. "Active tabs" means sessions currently open in the sidebar; "pinned" means pinned=true on disk. Both are kept. The key name is a slug of an older, softer English sentence — translate the current value, not the key.
entries.apps.designCritique.utils.i_ll_pull_the_: Design Critique composer, second half of the line said back about a pasted Figma link; the localised word for a Figma file and a middle dot come first, so this continues that line rather than opening one. "Frames" is Figma's own term for the artboards inside a file.
entries.apps.designCritique.utils.i_ll_clone_it_: Follows the localised word for a code repository and a middle dot in the Design Critique composer. "Screens" means app screens, never physical displays, and the second sentence is a limit rather than an error: a page needing a running server cannot be looked at.
entries.apps.designCritique.utils.i_ll_list_the_: Same limit as the repository variant but for a folder on this machine, and it drops the promise to clone because nothing is downloaded. Follows the localised words for local code and a middle dot.
entries.apps.designCritique.utils.it_must_be_run: Follows the localised words for the user's own dev server and a middle dot, which is why the English begins lower-case and reads as a continuation. The subject of "it" is that server, and "capture" means take a screenshot of the page as it is served.
entries.apps.designCritique.utils.i_ll_capture_i: The deployed-page counterpart of the dev-server tail, following the localised words for a live page and a middle dot. It omits the must-be-running warning because a deployed page is assumed up.
entries.apps.designCritique.utils.not_something_: The only one of these tails on the error path: it follows the localised word for Unrecognised and an em dash, and lists the four kinds of reference the field accepts. A pasted string matched none of them.
entries.apps.designCritique.scopingPicker.critiq: Label of the button that starts a critique on the scoping step, after the user has picked two or more of the discovered screens to audit as one flow. The count is how many are picked.
Label of the button that starts a critique on the scoping step, when exactly one of the discovered screens is picked.
entries.apps.designCritique.scopingPicker.pick_a: Disabled label of the scoping step's start button, shown while the user has picked nothing yet. It says what to do next, not what the button does.
entries.components.gitPanel.title: Title of the Git side panel showing the project repository state (branch, uncommitted changes, recent commits). "Git" is the version-control tool's proper name - do not translate.
entries.hooks.usePanelTabs.git: Tab label for the Git side-panel view in the chat right panel. "Git" is the version-control tool's proper name - do not translate.
entries.pages.chat.sidePanel.menu_git: Menu entry in the side panel "+" menu that opens the Git view. "Git" is the version-control tool's proper name - do not translate.
entries.components.selectionToolbar.copy: Button on the floating toolbar over selected chat text: copies the selection to the clipboard. A VERB ("copy this"), not the noun "a copy" — several languages use different words for the two. Sits in a row of short buttons, so keep it brief.
entries.components.selectionToolbar.quote: Button on the floating toolbar over selected chat text: inserts the selection into the main composer as a quotation to reply to. A VERB ("quote this"), not the noun "a quote" and not a price quotation. Sits in a row of short buttons, so keep it brief.
entries.components.selectionToolbar.ask: Button on the floating toolbar that appears over selected chat text, beside Quote and Copy: sends the selection to the Side Chat panel as a question, without touching the main conversation. "Ask" is a VERB, not the noun ("an ask"), and "Side Chat" is the panel's own name, so translate it the same way as pages.chat.sidePanel.menu_side. It sits in a row of short buttons -- if the full phrase does not fit your language, drop the panel name rather than abbreviating it into something unrecognisable.
entries.apps.commandBar.kind.app: Right-aligned kind label on a Command Bar row, in a column with "Command", "Setting" and "View". Short for a Kiro Crew APP -- an installed extension such as Dev Fleet or Meetings -- so the row opens that app, not a generic program and not a mobile app. A noun naming what the row is. Keep it short: the label shares the row with the title and subtitle and is the first thing truncated.
